turns: How do I authenticate server-to-server requests to the Northstar API with an API key? Which header do I use? Name the source document.
text:
To authenticate server-to-server requests to the Northstar API with an API key, use the **Authorization** header.

Include your API key in the header as follows:

```
Authorization: Bearer {NorthstarApiKey}
```

(Replace `{NorthstarApiKey}` with your actual API key.)

**Source document:** api_authentication_guide.html

API Authentication Guide Northstar Technologies Developer Documentation Last updated: June 2023 | API Version: 2.3 Table of Contents Overview API Key Authentication OAuth 2.0 JWT Tokens Security Best Practices Troubleshooting Overview The Northstar API supports multiple authentication methods to accommodate different use cases and security requirements. All API requests must be authenticated using one of the following methods: API Keys - Best for server-to-server integrations OAuth 2.0 - Best for user-facing applications JWT Tokens - Best for microservices and short-lived sessions Base URL: All API requests should be made to https://api.northstartech.com/v2 API Key Authentication API keys provide a simple way to authenticate server-to-server requests. Each API key is associated with a specific account and has configurable permissions. Generating an API Key Log in to the Northstar Dashboard Navigate to Settings → API Keys Click Generate New Key Select the appropriate permissions for your use case Copy and securely store your API key (it will only be shown once) Using API Keys Include your API key in the Authorization header: curl -X GET "https://api.northstartech.com/v2/users" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer ns_live_abc123xyz789" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" API Key Types

JWT Token Authentication JSON Web Tokens (JWT) can be used for short-lived authentication, particularly useful for microservices architectures.
